devon: quick heads-up — saw 3 ECC/Xid events in us-west-2 over the last 24h. Two nodes degraded and auto-drain kicked in. Suspect a cluster of older cards starting to go flaky. :eyes:

alex: ugh. do we have failure-rate per GPU-hour? breakdown by sku and age?

devon: pulling numbers now. preliminary: ~0.45 failures per 1k gpu-hours for a100-v1 (deployed 2021-22 fleet), ~0.12/1k for a100-v2 (newer). those 3 events were all on a100-v1 racks.

maria: ok — for capacity planning we should move from a flat "X spare nodes" rule to a probabilistic buffer. if p = failures per gpu-hour, and fleet has G GPUs, expected failures per hour = p*G. target spare buffer should cover tail (e.g., 99.5th percentile) for expected simultaneous failures during our replacement window.

alex: can you sketch the calc? just a tiny snippet or rule-of-thumb we can use in runbooks.

maria: sure. rough poisson model in one line: 
```
lambda = p * G * T_window  # expected failures over replacement window
spare_needed = poisson_quantile(0.995, lambda)  # numeric lookup
```
T_window = time to detect+drain+replace (hrs). if detection ~0.25h + replace ~2h => T_window~2.25h. for our us-west-2 a100-v1 rack (G=200, p=0.00045) lambda ~= 0.00045*200*2.25 = 0.2025 => 99.5% quantile ~2.

jin: that matches what we saw (spike of 2 simultaneous degradations). also flag: flaky cards often show rising corrected ECC counts hours before Xid. recommend we add an intermediate "pre-fail" metric to auto-tag nodes for accelerated replacement. ran a memtest sweep last night, flagged 7 nodes with ECC spikes.

alex: so practical recommendation? % buffer per region and per deployment tier (hosted vs dedicated)? cost tradeoffs?

maria: proposal: for older SKUs (a100-v1) keep N+3 redundancy for small pools (<50 GPUs), and 3% fleet buffer for large pools, scaled up to 5% for regions with older hardware or higher observed p. For newer SKUs keep 1.5% buffer, but monitor rolling 30d failure rate with weekly re-eval.

devon: adding to cost side: each spare GPU costs ~ $X/hr (inc infra amortized). moving from 2%->4% in us-west-2 increases monthly cost by ~12%. but unavailability costs (failed requests, degraded latency) are higher for Dedicated customers. tradeoff favors larger buffer for Dedicated.

infra-oncall-bot: [auto] Node i-gpu-172 flagged for ECC spike, cordoning and scheduling replacement. Ticket #INF-4872 created.

jin: action items: 1) enable ECC-corrected trend alert (rate-of-change) -> auto-tag pre-fail ; 2) run fleet memtest sweep weekly for 2 weeks targeting a100-v1 racks; 3) apply buffer policy: us-west-2 a100-v1 -> 4% initial buffer, re-eval in 14d; 4) add calculator to docs (link to spreadsheet in next message).

alex: +1 to all. devon, can infra ops own the replace schedule and cost calc? I'll draft the runbook template and spreadsheet model.

devon: owning replacement schedule. i'll spin up a quick calc and link the sheet here. also will start a short maintenance wave for the 7 flagged nodes tonight (low-traffic window).

maria: thanks — also note: for multi-region routing we can borrow capacity from eu-west-1 during peak us-west-2 drain windows if latency budget allows. that's cheaper than overprovisioning in every region. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

devon: noted. tagging this thread with action items + will post sheet link once ready. closing loop after tonight's maintenance. :white_check_mark:
